decisions.title: RustOS-only OS assembler; build-time modular selection
Configuration file and CLI first; graphical selection deferred
Emulator M1; Zero 2 W M2; Pi 5 later
One application with six internal ownership boundaries
Validate first; isolate runs; preserve outputs; report failures and cleanup
Show requirements, decisions, workflows and progress in dashboard
One delivery milestone; maximum two active items: primary plus research
M1 uses native Windows, QEMU virt and Cortex-A53 with bare-metal AArch64 soft-float
TOML with separate user config, target profile and module catalog; repository-local inputs first
Four CLI operations: validate, plan, build, verify; physical media writing separate
Confirmed separate hashed test kernels, exact markers, ten-second deadline, owned cleanup, and no-replacement publication
Report/manifest and EL1 kernel startup contracts approved as implementation baselines
Explicit repo discovery, owned Windows Job Objects/QMP lifecycle and bounded output approved
Approved M1 profile 0.1.1: instruction_counting=auto maps to -icount shift=auto
M2 PL011 transmit-only diagnostics; Pi BSP owns GPIO and firmware clock setup
M2 explicit boot memory, separate EL2-to-EL1 entry and one active core
M2 separate normal/panic 64 MiB MBR/FAT32 images and independent inspection
M2 strict versioned target/contracts, one board, locked assets and separate image/hardware evidence
M2 pinned real firmware/DTB assets with reproduced source archive and licence sidecar
Honor narrow dynamic CMA request with a reserved pool; retain stackless safety before private stack use
Cortex-A53 EL1 control baseline and explicit pre-BSS Rust validator ABI
Bounded mailbox UART clock setup, lifetime-long buffers, measured-rate validation and GPIO/PL011 order
Final variant token: bounded prefix drain followed by LF commit, with host-observed last-byte delivery
